context_edits.new: * covariance matrix. The diagonal entries {@code C[i][i]} are obtained * from a Cholesky decomposition of JTJ.

ownership_reason: Only the gold turns the normal matrix into the parameters' deviations: hop 1 multiplies them by the residual factor sqrt(chiSquare / (observations - parameters)) that its javadoc states, hop 2 passes the weighted Jacobian along, hop 3 forms J^T J exactly as computeCovariances does, hop 4 passes its entries on. The gold equilibrates the normal matrix, takes its inverse by QR and derives each deviation from the diagonal of the inverse; the variant omits the division by the parameter's scale, so it returns sqrt(A[i][i] * inverse(A)[i][i]), which is invariant under any rescaling of the parameters: no caller can pre-scale its input to recover the deviations, and recovering them afterwards needs a second, per-parameter implementation of the gold's step. The gold's javadoc promises the standard deviation of each parameter, the square root of the diagonal entry of the covariance matrix inverse(J^T J). The convention is pinned outside the gold: the facade's javadoc (sd(a[i]) = sqrt(S / (n - m) * C[i][i]), C the covariance matrix), the intact computeSigma of the same class (sqrt(cov[i][i])), the intact computeCovariances (C = QR inverse of J^T J) and the intact sibling optim.nonlinear.vector.jacobian.AbstractLeastSquaresOptimizer.computeSigma; the testCircleFitting covariance checks, the sibling's testCircleFitting2 (computeSigma on the same circle problem) and testComputeSigma (Kirby2, NIST certified deviations) pass.
